```{r}

# Load required packages
library(linkET)
library(vegan)
library(phyloseq)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)

# 1. Your working Bray-Curtis distance matrix
bray_dist_taxonomy <- phyloseq::distance(ps_RA, method = "bray")

# 2. Prepare environmental data (from your code)
env_df <- meta[, variables]
#env_df <- as.data.frame(lapply(env_df, as.numeric))

env_df <- env_df[, c(1, 2, 3, 11, 4, 13, 5, 9, 10, 12, 8, 6, 7, 14, 15)]
```






lets run this For taxonomy only

```{r}
# Load required packages
library(linkET)
library(vegan)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)

# 1. Your working Mantel test code with NA handling
mantel_results <- data.frame()

for (i in 1:ncol(env_df)) {
  env_dist <- dist(env_df[, i])
  
  m_test <- mantel(bray_dist_taxonomy, env_dist, 
                   method = "pearson",
                   permutations = 999,
                   na.rm = TRUE)
  
  mantel_results <- rbind(mantel_results,
                         data.frame(
                           variable = colnames(env_df)[i],
                           r = m_test$statistic,
                           p = m_test$signif
                         ))
}

# 2. Adjust p-values
mantel_results$p_adj <- p.adjust(mantel_results$p, method = "BH")

# 3. Format EXACTLY as geom_couple() expects
mantel_for_plot <- mantel_results %>%
  # Create spec column (microbiome group)
  mutate(spec = "Prokaryotic\ncommunity",
         # Create env column (must match correlation matrix names EXACTLY)
         env = variable,
         # Create rd factor with YOUR desired categories
         rd = case_when(
           abs(r) > 0.4 ~ ">0.4",
           abs(r) >= 0.3 ~ "0.3-0.4",
           abs(r) >= 0.2 ~ "0.2-0.3",
           abs(r) >= 0.1 ~ "0.1-0.2",
           TRUE ~ "<0.1"
         ),
         rd = factor(rd, levels = c("<0.1", "0.1-0.2", "0.2-0.3", "0.3-0.4", ">0.4")),
         # Create pd factor as in tutorial
         pd = case_when(
           p_adj < 0.01 ~ "< 0.01",
           p_adj < 0.05 ~ "0.01 - 0.05",
           TRUE ~ ">= 0.05"
         ),
         pd = factor(pd, levels = c("< 0.01", "0.01 - 0.05", ">= 0.05"))
  ) %>%
  # Select columns in the right order
  dplyr::select(spec, env, r, p, rd, pd)

print("Mantel data for geom_couple:")
print(mantel_for_plot)

# 4. Create correlation matrix with pairwise completion for NAs
env_cor_matrix <- cor(env_df, 
                      use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
                      method = "pearson")

# Replace any remaining NAs with 0 (for visualization only)
env_cor_matrix[is.na(env_cor_matrix)] <- 0

# 5. Create the plot EXACTLY like tutorial
p <- qcorrplot(env_cor_matrix, 
               type = "lower", 
               diag = FALSE,
               is_corr = TRUE) +  # Explicitly state it's a correlation matrix
  geom_square() +
  geom_couple(aes(colour = pd, size = rd), 
              data = mantel_for_plot, 
              curvature = nice_curvature(),
              key_glyph = "path") +  # Add this to control legend appearance
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 4, 6)) +  # 5 values for 5 categories
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("< 0.01" = "#D55E00",
                                 "0.01 - 0.05" = "#0EA271",
                                 ">= 0.05" = "grey35")) +
  guides(
    size = guide_legend(title = "Mantel's r",
                       override.aes = list(colour = "grey35", 
                                           linewidth = c(0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 4, 6)),  # 5 values to match categories
                       order = 2),
    colour = guide_legend(title = "Mantel's p (FDR)", 
                         override.aes = list(size = 1.5,  # Thicker lines
                                             linewidth = 1.5),  # Additional control
                         order = 1),
    fill = guide_colorbar(title = "Pearson's r", order = 3)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.key.size = unit(1.5, "lines")  # Increase legend key size
  ) + theme(
  plot.title = element_blank(),
  axis.title.x = element_blank(),
  axis.title.y = element_blank())

print(p)

```

PARTIAL MANTEL controlling for depth (numerical)

Run partial mantel

```{r}
# Load required packages
library(linkET)
library(vegan)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(ppcor)  # For partial correlations

# Use the numerical Depth column from meta
depth_numerical <- meta$`Depth (numerical)`

# Check that it's numeric
if(!is.numeric(depth_numerical)) {
  depth_numerical <- as.numeric(as.character(depth_numerical))
  warning("Converted Depth to numeric")
}

# First, ensure all distance matrices have matching samples
common_samples <- Reduce(intersect, list(
  labels(bray_dist_taxonomy),
  labels(bray_dist_KEGG),
  labels(bray_dist_CAZyme),
  meta$sampleID
))

print(paste("Number of common samples:", length(common_samples)))

# Function to subset distance matrices
subset_dist <- function(dist_obj, common_samples) {
  mat <- as.matrix(dist_obj)
  mat_subset <- mat[common_samples, common_samples]
  return(as.dist(mat_subset))
}

# Subset all distance matrices
bray_dist_taxonomy_sub <- subset_dist(bray_dist_taxonomy, common_samples)
bray_dist_KEGG_sub <- subset_dist(bray_dist_KEGG, common_samples)
bray_dist_CAZyme_sub <- subset_dist(bray_dist_CAZyme, common_samples)

# Create depth distance matrix from numerical Depth
depth_vector <- depth_numerical[match(common_samples, meta$sampleID)]

# Check for NAs in depth
if(any(is.na(depth_vector))) {
  print(paste("Found", sum(is.na(depth_vector)), "NAs in depth. Removing those samples."))
  valid_depth <- !is.na(depth_vector)
  depth_vector <- depth_vector[valid_depth]
  common_samples <- common_samples[valid_depth]
  
  # Resubset distance matrices
  bray_dist_taxonomy_sub <- subset_dist(bray_dist_taxonomy, common_samples)
  bray_dist_KEGG_sub <- subset_dist(bray_dist_KEGG, common_samples)
  bray_dist_CAZyme_sub <- subset_dist(bray_dist_CAZyme, common_samples)
}

depth_dist <- dist(depth_vector)

# Remove Depth from env_df BEFORE subsetting
env_df_no_depth <- env_df[, !colnames(env_df) %in% c("Depth (numerical)")]
env_df_sub <- env_df_no_depth[common_samples, , drop = FALSE]

# Create a list of all communities
communities <- list(
  Taxonomy = bray_dist_taxonomy_sub,
  KEGG = bray_dist_KEGG_sub,
  CAZyme = bray_dist_CAZyme_sub
)

# Run Partial Mantel tests controlling for depth
mantel_all_results <- data.frame()

for (community_name in names(communities)) {
  bray_dist <- communities[[community_name]]
  
  for (i in 1:ncol(env_df_sub)) {
    variable_name <- colnames(env_df_sub)[i]
    
    # Get the environmental variable
    env_var <- env_df_sub[, i]
    
    # Find samples with non-NA values for this variable 
    complete_idx <- which(!is.na(env_var))
    
    if(length(complete_idx) < 3) {
      next
    }
    
    # Subset all matrices to complete cases
    bray_mat <- as.matrix(bray_dist)
    bray_sub <- bray_mat[complete_idx, complete_idx]
    bray_dist_sub <- as.dist(bray_sub)
    
    depth_sub <- depth_vector[complete_idx]
    depth_dist_sub <- dist(depth_sub)
    
    env_dist_sub <- dist(env_var[complete_idx])
    
    # Run partial Mantel test
    result <- tryCatch({
      m_test <- mantel.partial(bray_dist_sub, env_dist_sub, depth_dist_sub,
                               method = "pearson",
                               permutations = 999,
                               na.rm = TRUE)
      
      data.frame(
        community = community_name,
        variable = variable_name,
        r = m_test$statistic,
        p = m_test$signif,
        n_used = length(complete_idx),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }, error = function(e) {
      cat("Error in", community_name, variable_name, ":", e$message, "\n")
      NULL
    })
    
    if(!is.null(result)) {
      mantel_all_results <- rbind(mantel_all_results, result)
    }
  }
}

# Adjust p-values separately for each community
mantel_all_results <- mantel_all_results %>%
  group_by(community) %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup()

print("All Partial Mantel results (controlling for depth):")
print(mantel_all_results)

# Calculate PARTIAL correlations among environmental variables (controlling for depth)
# AND their significance
env_vars <- colnames(env_df_sub)
n_vars <- length(env_vars)
partial_cor_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = n_vars, ncol = n_vars)
partial_p_matrix <- matrix(1, nrow = n_vars, ncol = n_vars)  # For p-values
rownames(partial_cor_matrix) <- env_vars
colnames(partial_cor_matrix) <- env_vars
rownames(partial_p_matrix) <- env_vars
colnames(partial_p_matrix) <- env_vars

# Calculate partial correlations and p-values for each pair
for (i in 1:n_vars) {
  for (j in 1:n_vars) {
    if (i == j) {
      partial_cor_matrix[i, j] <- 1
      partial_p_matrix[i, j] <- 0
    } else if (i > j) {  # Only calculate once for each pair
      # Find samples with complete data for both variables AND depth
      complete_idx <- which(!is.na(env_df_sub[, i]) & 
                            !is.na(env_df_sub[, j]) & 
                            !is.na(depth_vector))
      
      if(length(complete_idx) > 3) {
        # Create data frame with the two variables and depth
        df_partial <- data.frame(
          x = env_df_sub[complete_idx, i],
          y = env_df_sub[complete_idx, j],
          z = depth_vector[complete_idx]
        )
        
        # Calculate partial correlation and p-value
        tryCatch({
          pcor_test <- pcor.test(df_partial$x, df_partial$y, df_partial$z)
          partial_cor_matrix[i, j] <- pcor_test$estimate
          partial_cor_matrix[j, i] <- pcor_test$estimate
          partial_p_matrix[i, j] <- pcor_test$p.value
          partial_p_matrix[j, i] <- pcor_test$p.value
        }, error = function(e) {
          # If error, use regular correlation
          cat("Warning: Using regular correlation for", env_vars[i], "and", env_vars[j], "\n")
          cor_test <- cor.test(df_partial$x, df_partial$y, use = "complete.obs")
          partial_cor_matrix[i, j] <- cor_test$estimate
          partial_cor_matrix[j, i] <- cor_test$estimate
          partial_p_matrix[i, j] <- cor_test$p.value
          partial_p_matrix[j, i] <- cor_test$p.value
        })
      } else {
        # If insufficient data, use regular correlation with a warning
        cat("Warning: Insufficient data for partial correlation between", 
            env_vars[i], "and", env_vars[j], "- using regular correlation\n")
        cor_test <- cor.test(env_df_sub[, i], env_df_sub[, j], 
                             use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
        partial_cor_matrix[i, j] <- cor_test$estimate
        partial_cor_matrix[j, i] <- cor_test$estimate
        partial_p_matrix[i, j] <- cor_test$p.value
        partial_p_matrix[j, i] <- cor_test$p.value
      }
    }
  }
}

# Adjust p-values for multiple testing (optional)
partial_p_matrix_adj <- matrix(p.adjust(partial_p_matrix, method = "BH"), 
                               nrow = n_vars, ncol = n_vars)
rownames(partial_p_matrix_adj) <- env_vars
colnames(partial_p_matrix_adj) <- env_vars

# Create a matrix for significance stars
sig_stars <- matrix("", nrow = n_vars, ncol = n_vars)
sig_stars[partial_p_matrix_adj < 0.001] <- "***"
sig_stars[partial_p_matrix_adj < 0.01 & partial_p_matrix_adj >= 0.001] <- "**"
sig_stars[partial_p_matrix_adj < 0.05 & partial_p_matrix_adj >= 0.01] <- "*"
sig_stars[partial_p_matrix_adj < 0.1 & partial_p_matrix_adj >= 0.05] <- "."
# Leave empty for non-significant

# Format Mantel results for plotting
mantel_for_plot <- mantel_all_results %>%
  mutate(spec = community,
         env = variable,
         rd = case_when(
           abs(r) >= 0.4 ~ "≥0.4",
           abs(r) >= 0.2 ~ "0.2-0.4",
           TRUE ~ "<0.2"
         ),
         rd = factor(rd, levels = c("<0.2", "0.2-0.4", "≥0.4")),
         pd = case_when(
           p_adj < 0.01 ~ "< 0.01",
           p_adj < 0.05 ~ "0.01 - 0.05",
           TRUE ~ ">= 0.05"
         ),
         pd = factor(pd, levels = c("< 0.01", "0.01 - 0.05", ">= 0.05"))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(spec, env, r, p, rd, pd)

###############

```

```{r}
# Create a matrix for significance stars
sig_stars <- matrix("", nrow = n_vars, ncol = n_vars)
sig_stars[partial_p_matrix_adj < 0.001] <- "***"
sig_stars[partial_p_matrix_adj < 0.01 & partial_p_matrix_adj >= 0.001] <- "**"
sig_stars[partial_p_matrix_adj < 0.05 & partial_p_matrix_adj >= 0.01] <- "*"
sig_stars[partial_p_matrix_adj < 0.1 & partial_p_matrix_adj >= 0.05] <- "."

# Set upper triangle (including diagonal) to empty strings
sig_stars[upper.tri(sig_stars, diag = TRUE)] <- ""

# Convert to data frame with correct coordinates
sig_stars_df <- data.frame(
  x = rep(1:n_vars, each = n_vars),
  y = rep(1:n_vars, times = n_vars),
  label = as.vector(sig_stars),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Filter out empty labels
sig_stars_df <- sig_stars_df[sig_stars_df$label != "", ]

# Ensure we only keep lower triangle (since plot type = "lower")
sig_stars_df <- sig_stars_df[sig_stars_df$y > sig_stars_df$x, ]

# Map the numeric coordinates to variable names for proper labeling
sig_stars_df$x_name <- env_vars[sig_stars_df$x]
sig_stars_df$y_name <- env_vars[sig_stars_df$y]

# Create the plot with partial correlations and significance stars
p <- qcorrplot(partial_cor_matrix, 
               type = "lower", 
               diag = FALSE,
               is_corr = TRUE) +
  geom_square() +
  # Add significance stars - changed size from 5 to 3.5
  geom_text(data = sig_stars_df,
            aes(x = x_name, y = y_name, label = label),
            color = "black", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", 
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_couple(aes(colour = pd, size = rd), 
              data = mantel_for_plot, 
              curvature = nice_curvature()) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(0.5, 1, 2)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("< 0.01" = "#8508DA",
                                 "0.01 - 0.05" = "#E08D06",
                                 ">= 0.05" = "grey35")) +
  guides(
    size = guide_legend(title = "Partial Mantel's r\n(controlling for depth)",
                       override.aes = list(colour = "grey35"), 
                       order = 2),
    colour = guide_legend(title = "Partial Mantel's p (FDR)\n (controlling for depth)", 
                         override.aes = list(size = 3), 
                         order = 1),
    fill = guide_colorbar(title = "Partial Pearson's r\n(controlling for depth)", 
                         order = 3)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    # Remove all grid lines
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    # Remove white background
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    # Optional: add a subtle border if you want
    # panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "grey80", size = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),  # Remove axis ticks if you want cleaner look
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
  )

print(p)


```
